extra.message: The handler builds an exception message containing the internal filesystem path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR) and user input, then returns str(exc) and the exception class name to the client. This leaks server paths and implementation details (CWE-209).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The full request body and the Authorization header are written to the application log via logger.warning, exposing credentials and sensitive payloads to anyone with log access (CWE-532).

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The user-controlled 'lane' query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse without validation, allowing an attacker to redirect users to an arbitrary external site (open redirect / phishing) (CWE-601).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Untrusted request data (raw body or base64-decoded blob) is deserialized with pickle.loads(), enabling arbitrary code execution on the server when a malicious pickle payload is supplied (CWE-502).

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: Arbitrary JSON is merged into the workset via dict.update(payload), letting the client override role, tier, approved and balance fields, resulting in privilege escalation and tampering with financial/approval state (CWE-915).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The user-controlled 'ref' parameter is concatenated into a filesystem path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json") without normalization, enabling path traversal and arbitrary file write outside the intended export directory (CWE-22).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: Social Security numbers and credit card numbers from the request are written to disk in cleartext without encryption or masking, exposing PII/PCI data (CWE-312).

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: MD5 is used to hash user-supplied input. MD5 is cryptographically broken and must not be used for security-sensitive hashing (CWE-327).

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: The 'count' query parameter is used to allocate a list of arbitrary size with no upper bound, allowing an attacker to exhaust server memory/CPU (denial of service) (CWE-770).

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: A user-controlled 'endpoint' URL is fetched with urllib.request.urlopen(), allowing Server-Side Request Forgery against internal services and cloud metadata endpoints (CWE-918).

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: Authentication verifier values are hardcoded in source ({"north": "4812", "south": "5930"}). Anyone with source access can authenticate as a known handle (CWE-798).

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The endpoint reflects an arbitrary Origin header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, allowing any malicious site to read credentialed cross-origin responses (CWE-942).

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The user-controlled 'fragment' parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 template and rendered, enabling Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) and remote code execution (CWE-1336/CWE-94).

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code

extra.message: Elevated privileges are granted solely because the client-controlled 'ops_badge' cookie/header equals 'lead'. Any client can set this value, bypassing authentication and authorization (CWE-807/CWE-287).

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
CWE-287: Improper Authentication

extra.message: The user-controlled 'host' parameter is concatenated into a shell command passed to os.system(), allowing OS command injection and arbitrary command execution (CWE-78).

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: Security codes are generated with the non-cryptographic 'random' module, making them predictable and unsuitable for security tokens (CWE-338).

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: The user-controlled JSON 'filter' is passed directly to MongoDB find_one(), allowing NoSQL operator injection (e.g. {"$ne": null}) to bypass query logic and read arbitrary records (CWE-943).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The user-controlled 'name' parameter is used to build the destination path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) and the raw request body is written there, enabling path traversal and arbitrary file write (CWE-22).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The lxml parser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True and no_network=False on user-supplied XML, enabling XML External Entity (XXE) attacks including local file disclosure and SSRF (CWE-611).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The unauthenticated /api/auth/register endpoint accepts a client-supplied 'role' and stores it directly (role=user_in.role). An attacker can register as PROPERTY_ADMIN and gain full administrative access (CWE-269).

cwe: CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management
CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: The authentication cookie carrying the JWT is set without the Secure attribute (only httponly and samesite are set), so the token can be sent over plain HTTP and intercepted (CWE-614).

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: Password reset tokens are printed to the console/log in plaintext. Anyone with log access can use the token against /api/auth/password-reset-confirm to hijack accounts (CWE-532).

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The /api/auth/login endpoint has no rate limiting, throttling or account lockout, permitting unlimited password guessing and credential stuffing (CWE-307). The password-reset endpoints share the same gap.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: After a password reset the user's password hash is changed but existing JWTs are not invalidated. A previously stolen token remains valid until its 480-minute expiry (CWE-613).

cwe: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

extra.message: A hardcoded default JWT signing secret ('change-me-in-production-dev-only-key') is embedded in source. If not overridden via the environment, an attacker can forge valid JWTs and impersonate any user, including admins (CWE-798).

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: update_ticket has no require_role() check; it only verifies can_view_maintenance_ticket, which an assigned MAINTENANCE_WORKER passes. The unrestricted setattr loop then lets the worker modify any field including assigned_to, priority, title and description (CWE-862).

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: get_message enforces ownership only for the TENANT role. MAINTENANCE_WORKER, PROPERTY_MANAGER and PROPERTY_ADMIN have no access-control check and can read any message by ID, including private conversations across properties (IDOR, CWE-639).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: list_replies performs no access-control check on the parent message. Any authenticated user can read all replies (internal notes are only filtered for tenants) to arbitrary messages by ID (CWE-639).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: upload_inspection_photo has no require_role() gate and relies only on can_view_inspection, which tenants pass for their own unit. Tenants can therefore add/modify inspection photo evidence on records they should only be able to view (CWE-862).

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: create_lease validates unit_id against the manager's managed properties but never validates tenant_id. A PROPERTY_MANAGER can create leases that associate tenants from outside their managed properties, crossing data boundaries (CWE-639).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Imported tenant accounts are created with the hardcoded default password 'changeme123' when the CSV omits a password, enabling trivial account takeover of imported users (CWE-798).

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: User-controlled values (e.g. tenant full_name) are written to the CSV export without neutralizing leading formula characters (=, +, -, @). Opening the export in a spreadsheet can execute injected formulas (CSV/formula injection, CWE-1236).

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File
